Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the pre-operative image (Figure 1a), which shows a relatively clear mediastinum, with the post-operative image (Figure 3a), there is a marked increase in the width of the superior mediastinum and new right basal opacity. In the context of a patient with a history of goitre and dyspnoea, this rapid enlargement of the mediastinal mass shortly after surgery is highly suggestive of an aggressive malignancy such as thyroid angiosarcoma rather than a benign post-surgical change or successful removal.
